Table 1: Camouflage detection results: COD10K [13], CAMO [26], NC4K [38]. Baselines comprising domain-specific methods are marked with a dagger (†) Top-2 results are shown in bold, and top-5 results are underlined. Among our experiments, the best, second-best, and third-best results are highlighted in gold, silver, and bronze, respectively. Datasets marked with an asterisk (*) are evaluated in a zero-shot setting, i.e., they were not seen during model training.

Table 2: a) Remote sensing: EarthReason [27]. b) Reasoning segmentation results: ReasonSeg [25], ReasonSeg-R, ReasonSeg-X [66], where only baselines with backbones of similar size are reported. Baselines comprising domain-specific methods are marked with a dagger (†). Top-2 results are shown in bold, and top-5 results are underlined. Among our experiments, the best, second-best, and third-best results are highlighted in gold, silver, and bronze, respectively. Datasets marked with an asterisk (*) are evaluated in a zero-shot setting, i.e., they were not seen during model training.

Figure 7: Evaluation performance for reasoning segmentation trainings. Tracked metric is mean between gIoU and cIoU. Best checkpoint is marked with a star. For bootstrapped runs the evaluations of the GRTO stage are reported. The cost of bootstrapping is negligible compared to joint training.

Figure 4: a) Results of ablation studies conducted on EarthReason. b) B-GRPO gains compared to GRPO, against loss compared to B-GRTO. IoUs are computed on EarthReason validation and test splits, while camouflage metrics are computed on COD10K. Bootstrapping the tool, even without subsequent joint optimization, still leads to significant performance gains, although not as large as B-GRTO.

Figure 3: The Bootstrapped Group Relative Tool Optimization (B-GRTO) pipeline: first, the tool is bootstrapped off-policy with a replay buffer populated from the reference policy πθ0 and optimal importance sampling weights πθ∗/πθ0 [54] via BTO; then, the policy πθ and the tool are trained jointly to maximize expected reward via GRTO.
Figure 8: COD10K test set qualitative results. The red box in the image shows the ground-truth bounding box.

Figure 5: Evaluation performance for camouflage trainings. Tracked metric is weighted F-measure. Best checkpoint is marked with a star. For bootstrapped runs the evaluations of the GRTO stage are reported. The cost of bootstrapping is negligible compared to joint training.

Figure 6: Evaluation performance for remote sensing trainings. Tracked metric is mean between gIoU and cIoU. Best checkpoint is marked with a star. For bootstrapped runs the evaluations of the GRTO stage are reported. The cost of bootstrapping is negligible compared to joint training.
